name: content-generation-modules.human-sounding-writing
notes: Severity: error = must fix; warn = fix or justify in a comment; info = density signal only. Regexes are ECMAScript/Python-compatible (no lookbehind). 'scope' tells the linter what unit to test. Contrast rules are warn, not error: pickles.news argues banning 'not X but Y' at generation time can remove real reasoning, so apply them in an edit pass after drafting. Vendored into content-generation-modules for the human-sounding-writing module. Owned by CGM; original research corpus retained.

patterns.description: Negative parallelism: 'not X, but Y' / 'not only X but also Y' / 'not just X, it's Y'
patterns.fix: State Y directly. Keep a contrast only if it marks a real category boundary, max 1 per section.

patterns.description: Trailing contrast: 'X, not Y' (e.g. 'as results, not as footnotes')
patterns.fix: Drop the 'not Y' tail, or turn it into a concrete sentence about what you did.

patterns.description: 'Y rather than X' reframing (common in Grok output)
patterns.fix: Prefer a direct statement.

patterns.description: 'No X. No Y. Just Z.' fragment pattern
patterns.fix: Write one full sentence.

patterns.description: Title or heading built as 'Claim: reveal' or 'X is not enough: Y'
patterns.fix: Write one plain declarative sentence without a colon.

patterns.description: Title uses 'not enough', 'should', 'why X matters', 'the hidden cost'
patterns.regex: \b(?:is not enough|isn't enough|should also|why .{1,30} matters|the hidden (?:cost|truth)|what .{1,30} hides)\b
patterns.fix: State the finding: who did what, with a number.

patterns.description: Em dash overuse
patterns.fix: Use commas, periods or parentheses.

patterns.description: Rhythmic triplet: 'A, B, and C' (count per 1,000 words)
patterns.fix: Keep real lists of three; cut triplets used for rhythm; use two items or four when that's the truth.

patterns.description: Present-participle tail that adds fake analysis (', highlighting ...', ', reflecting ...')
patterns.fix: End the sentence at the fact. If the implication matters, give it its own sentence with evidence.

patterns.description: Any ', <verb>ing' participial clause (density check)
patterns.fix: Split into two sentences with a subject and a verb.

patterns.description: Stacked or vague hedges
patterns.regex: \b(?:may|might|could)\s+(?:potentially|possibly|perhaps)\b|\b(?:potentially|arguably|somewhat|relatively|fairly|generally|typically|to some extent|in some ways|it seems that|it appears that|tends? to suggest)\b
patterns.fix: Hedge once, with the actual limit ('on these 760 questions').

patterns.description: Signposting / throat-clearing
patterns.regex: \b(?:in this (?:section|paper|article|post),? we (?:will )?(?:discuss|explore|examine|delve|look at)|let'?s (?:take a (?:closer )?look|explore|dive)|here'?s (?:the thing|why|what)|the (?:real|key) question is|it turns out that|as we will see|as mentioned (?:above|earlier)|needless to say)\b
patterns.fix: Delete; start with the content.

patterns.description: Restating summary sentence
patterns.regex: ^(?:In (?:short|summary|conclusion|other words|sum)|Overall|Ultimately|Taken together|All in all|To sum up|The bottom line|Simply put)\b
patterns.fix: Delete the sentence if it repeats; end on the last new fact.

patterns.description: Formulaic 'Despite ..., X faces challenges / Despite these challenges'
patterns.fix: Name the specific limitation and its size.

patterns.description: Unattributed authority
patterns.fix: Cite a named source with a link.

patterns.description: 'serves as / stands as / represents' instead of 'is'
patterns.fix: Use 'is'.

patterns.description: Bullet that starts with a bold label and colon
patterns.fix: Write the bullet as a normal sentence, or use prose.

patterns.description: Title Case Heading (4+ capitalised words)
patterns.fix: Use sentence case.

patterns.description: Dismissive 'an X with Y and Z' formula
patterns.fix: Only keep if both Y and Z are literal facts.

patterns.description: Precise-looking time/percent attached to an unsupported claim (manual review)
patterns.fix: Check the number is from our results; otherwise cut it.

patterns.description: Internal IDs, file paths or version tags in body text
patterns.fix: Move to Methods; in body text describe the thing in words.

sentence_length_words.why: LLM prose has long, uniform sentences and few short punchy ones (Economist; stylometric uniformity cited by UZH). Plain-language guidance favours short sentences.

subject_verb_gap_words.why: Readers stall when the verb is far from its subject (Gopen & Swan).

first_person_required.why: A named narrator who made decisions is the thing AI drafts lack.

numbers_per_paragraph.why: Every claim should be earned by a number, a named model, or an example.

charts.check: title must contain a verb and either a number or a comparison word, and must not be a noun-phrase label
charts.target: svg: first <text> with class/role title, or JSON field 'title'

charts.check: no experiment IDs, file paths, script names or version tags in any visible text
charts.target: all visible <text>/<tspan> in SVG; title, subtitle, labels, annotations, footer in JSON

charts.check: no statistical jargon in title or subtitle
max 4 colour series/stack segments; max 3 colours plus grey
charts.target: count distinct fill colours of data marks (SVG) or len(series) (JSON)

charts.check: max 15 bars/rows in a main-text chart; otherwise show top N + highlight and move full list to a table
no separate legend element; every series has a text label within 40px of its marks, or series names appear colour-coded in the subtitle
charts.target: SVG: absence of <g class*='legend'>; JSON: legend == false

charts.check: main-text charts must not be dumbbell, error-bar/whisker, hollow-vs-filled dot, dual-axis, or pie with >5 slices
charts.target: JSON field 'type'; SVG heuristic: <line> joining two <circle> per row, or whisker caps

charts.check: ranking charts: bars ordered by value (largest first), not alphabetically or by internal ID
ranking -> ordered bar; part-to-whole (right/wrong/skipped shares) -> 100% stacked bar; bars for counts and percentages of a whole, dots/strips when showing a mean with spread
every reference line has a label of >=4 words that explains it (not just 'baseline 50.3%')
footer starts with 'Source:' and names a dataset a reader can find (link), not a script
a 1-3 sentence text description of the takeaway sits directly under the chart in the page body
at most 1 decimal place in labels
